questions.question: What is the difference between the compound interest on ₹40,000 at 20% per annum compounded half - yearly and compounded quarterly for a period of one year ?
questions.solution:
Calculation of compound interest for half-yearly CI₁ = P(1 + r₁/100)²ⁿ - P

Calculation of compound interest for quarterly of year CI₂ = P(1 + r₂/100)⁴ⁿ - P

Given :

Principle = 40,000

Rate of interest = 20%

∴ r₁ for half-yearly = 10%

∴ r₂ for quarterly of year = 5%

⇒ n = 1 year

Difference between the compound interest on ₹40,000 at 20% per annum compounded half - yearly and compounded quarterly for a period of one year is :

⇒ CI₁ -CI₂ = [P(1 + r1/100)2n - P] - [P(1 + r2/100)4n - P]

⇒ P(1 + 10/100)² - P - P(1 + 5/100)⁴ + P

⇒ P(1 + 1/10)² - P(1 + 1/20)⁴

= 40000(11/10)² - 40000(21/20)⁴

= 40000[(11/10)² - (21/20)⁴]

or

= 40000 [(21/20)⁴ - (11/10)²]

= 40000(1.05⁴ - 1.1²)

= 40000(1.21550625 - 1.21)

= 40000 (0.00550625)

**= 220.25**

Hence, the correct answer is **"₹ 220.25".**

questions.question: The statutory power for exchange control was provided to Reserve Bank of India by the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act (FERA) of _______, which was subsequently replaced by a more comprehensive Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1973.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __1947__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Exchange control was introduced in India under the Defence of India Rules on September 3, 1939, on a temporary basis.
 
• The statutory power for exchange control was provided by the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act (FERA) of 1947, which was subsequently replaced by a more comprehensive Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1973. 
 
• Liberalization was introduced in 1991 and this Act was amended as a new Foreign Exchange Regulation (Amendment) Act 1993. 
 
• Significant developments in the external sector, such as a substantial increase in foreign exchange reserves, growth in foreign trade, rationalization of tariffs, current account convertibility, liberalization of Indian investments abroad, etc, resulted in a changing environment.
 
• In view of this changing environment, the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) was enacted in 1999 to replace FERA.
 
• FEMA became effective on June 1, 2000.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• FEMA aims at facilitating external trade and payments and for promoting the orderly development and maintenance of foreign exchange markets in India.
 
• Emphasizing the shift in focus, the Reserve Bank in due course also amended (since January 31, 2004) the name of its department dealing with the foreign exchange transactions to the Foreign Exchange Department from Exchange Control Department.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT true regarding 'Spring tides'?

options.text: These tides occur on new moon days.
These tides occur during full moon days.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**These tides are the lowest.**__

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****

__
 
• **Tides** refer to the rise and fall in sea levels caused by the combination of gravitational forces exerted by the Moon and the Sun and the rotation of the Earth.
 
• There are two types of Tides: **Spring Tides **and **Neap Tides.**
 
• **Spring Tides **occur when the Sun, the Moon, and the Earth are in a straight line.
 
• 
 
 
 **High tides are higher and low tides are lower than average. **

 
 
• Spring tides occur twice a month.
 
 
• **One during the full moon period** and
 
• **another during the new moon period.**
 
 
 
 

 
• **Neap Tides** occur when the Sun and the Moon are at right angles to each other and the forces of the sun and the moon tend to counteract one another.

 
 
• These tides also occur twice a month. However, there is a 7-day interval between Spring and Neap tides.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Spring tides** are the tide just after a new or full moon, when there is the greatest difference between high and low water.
 
• So the difference between the new moon and full moon is 15 days. Hence the tides are fortnightly.
 
• In New Moon Syzygy, the high-high tide at a position will be higher than the high-high tide on the same position during Full Moon Syzygy.
 
• It is so because, in the new moon syzygy, the moon is between the Sun and Earth.
 
• So there will be a combined direct pull of the Sun and moon on that face of the earth.
 
• **Hence a higher high-high tide.**

• In cell culture, it is used to study the growth, differentiation, and migration of cells.

•

• Cooperative Societies are formed for the mutual benefit of its members. Hence, the Credit Cooperative Society provides low-cost finance or cheap credit to its members at very nominal rate of interest. 
 
• Example of Credit Cooperative Society - **Krishak Cooperative**
 
• Krishak Cooperative provides loans for construction of houses, fishery loans, loans for agricultural trade and cultivation, loans for the purchase of agricultural implements, and loans for a variety of other expenses.

• There shall be at least 7 members with a draft of Memorandum of Association to register a Cooperative Society.
 
• It is governed by a managing committee that is elected democratically by its members.

• It is mutually beneficial to members of low and middle-income groups.

The old man was __**too weak that he couldn't **__ climb the stairs.
questions.solution:

• So, the phrase **so weak to** or **option 1 **is negated.

• **​Very **is used to emphasize that the following description applies without qualification.
 
• **Too **is used to show a higher degree than is desirable, permissible, or possible; excessively.
 
• Thus, **too **is the best fit adverb to describe **weak **in the given context. 
 
 
 
• Hence the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence is **too weak to.** 
 
• So, **option 4 **is the ***correct answer. ***
